title: Owl Babies
author: Martin Waddell

hero.name: Owl Baby (Sarah, Percy, or Bill)
hero.description: Small fluffy baby owl, wide-eyed, sitting on a branch at night — as illustrated by Patrick Benson
hero.source_note: Generic baby owl symbol from Boardmaker should suffice; if a more book-accurate fluffy white owlet is needed, source from TPT or Creative Fabrica

ambiguous.issue: Could mean the adjective (absence of light) or the verb (to darken)
ambiguous.reason: In this book dark refers to the scary nighttime setting — use an image showing darkness or a dark sky

ambiguous.issue: Abstract concept — could be shown as people side by side or as a hug
ambiguous.reason: Reunion of the owl family at the end of the story — search for a symbol showing animals or figures grouped together

notes: Owl Babies centres on three baby owls — Sarah, Percy, and Bill — who wake to find their mother gone and anxiously wait for her return. The emotional arc (fear → relief → joy) is the core of the story, so 'scared', 'wait', 'come back', and 'happy' are high-priority fringe words. 'Together' captures the reunion ending ('And she came back'). The existing activity_images vocab already includes owl, tree, night, nest, moon, and branch — these overlap well; 'owl' and 'nest' and 'tree' and 'night' are retained in fringe because they are the most communicatively essential. The existing aac_extras 'wait' and 'come_back' align perfectly with this book's central repeated phrase ('She'll come back'). Consider pairing the board with a visual of the mother owl returning as a reward/motivator for waiting.

matching.note: Min 4 approved stems, no hard cap
